findings.title: limitFunction drops all caller arguments
findings.cause: The returned wrapper is zero-argument: `return () => limit(() => function_());`, so values passed to the limited function are never forwarded to the wrapped function.
findings.impact: Any real use of `limitFunction` with a parameterized function returns results for `undefined` inputs. This breaks the declared return type `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>` and the documented usage pattern where callers invoke the returned function with inputs.
findings.evidence: index.js:121-124 returns a no-arg wrapper. index.d.ts:133-136 declares the returned function as accepting the original function arguments. A focused runtime probe returned `limitFunctionArg: "missing"` for `await limitFunction(async value => value ?? 'missing', {concurrency: 1})('sentinel')`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add an AVA test: `const limited = limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1}); t.is(await limited('sentinel'), 'sentinel');`. It currently resolves to `undefined` or the fallback used by the wrapped function.

findings.title: limit.map omits indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: `map` checks `Array.isArray(iterable)` and passes `undefined` as the mapper index for Sets, generators, and other valid iterables.
findings.impact: The public contract says the mapper receives the item value and its index for any iterable. Consumers using Sets or generator iterables get `undefined` indexes despite the TypeScript signature requiring `index: number`.
findings.evidence: index.js:108-112 passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`. readme.md:78-84 and index.d.ts:30-43 specify index delivery for iterable mapping. A focused runtime probe returned `mapSetIndexes: ["missing", "missing", "missing"]` for a Set input.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add an AVA test: `const indexes = await pLimit(2).map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (_value, index) => index); t.deepEqual(indexes, [0, 1]);`. It currently produces `[undefined, undefined]`.

findings.title: Options-object form enables rejectOnClear by default despite documented default false
findings.cause: The options destructuring uses `rejectOnClear = true` when callers pass `{concurrency}`, overriding the module-level default of `false`.
findings.impact: `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` now rejects pending promises on `clearQueue()` even though docs and types say `rejectOnClear` defaults to `false`. This makes the numeric and object forms behave differently and can unexpectedly reject pending work in code that only switched to object syntax.
findings.evidence: index.js:4 initializes `rejectOnClear` to false, but index.js:6-7 changes the default to true for options objects. readme.md:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 both state default false. A runtime probe observed `optionsDefaultClearOutcome: "rejected:AbortError"` for `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` without `rejectOnClear`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Create a running task and one pending task with `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1});`, call `limit.clearQueue()`, and assert the pending promise remains unsettled like `pLimit(1)`. It currently rejects with `AbortError`.

findings.title: rejectOnClear accepts falsey non-boolean values
findings.cause: Validation only throws when `rejectOnClear` is truthy and not boolean: `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`.
findings.impact: Invalid configuration values such as `0`, `''`, and `null` are silently accepted, violating the documented boolean contract and hiding caller mistakes. Truthy invalid values still throw, so validation behavior is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: readme.md:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 define `rejectOnClear` as boolean. The focused runtime probe recorded `rejectOnClear_0: "accepted"`, `rejectOnClear_: "accepted"`, and `rejectOnClear_null: "accepted"`, while `'nope'` throws.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add an AVA test asserting `t.throws(() => pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0}), {instanceOf: TypeError});` and similarly for `null` or `''`. These are currently accepted.

findings.title: Infinity is rejected as a concurrency limit
findings.impact: The package no longer supports the unbounded concurrency mode represented by `Infinity`, even though the committed baseline allowed it and the public contract describes a number with minimum 1 rather than an integer-only subset. This can break callers that use `Infinity` to disable limiting without branching.
findings.evidence: index.js:127-129 rejects non-integers. `git show HEAD:index.js` shows the baseline validator accepted `(Number.isInteger(concurrency) || concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) && concurrency > 0`. A focused runtime probe printed `Infinity threw TypeError Expected \`concurrency\` to be a number from 1 and up`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add an AVA test: `const limit = pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY); t.is(limit.concurrency, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY); await Promise.all([limit(() => 1), limit(() => 2)]);`. Construction currently throws.
